clue.text: Title backed by old man's capital

parts.note: pa is an informal word for one's father, the old man

indicators.note: backed tells us the title word is read from the end to the start

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A title passed down from a father, as if inheriting his capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital city is the obvious instance of a capital.

clue.text: Demure Italian this writer's seen as simple

parts.note: prim means demure and proper
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth
this writer is the setter, I; I have becomes I've

explanation.surface: A modest Italian setter is thought of as naive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer's' is I'VE, since the 's here stands for has.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means simple and basic, undeveloped.

clue.text: Right sucker husband ditched fast!

indicators.note: ditched means the husband letter is thrown out of the sucker word

parts.note: an aphid is a sap-sucking insect

explanation.surface: A gullible fool quickly abandons her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' looks like a dupe but is a sap-sucking greenfly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and fast both mean quick.

clue.text: Loose stones on church pathway ultimately making harsh noise

parts.note: scree is loose stones on a mountainside

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word pathway

explanation.surface: Loose gravel on the church path crunches loudly underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Screechy describes a shrill, grating sound.

clue.text: Lively savage seizing heads of village assembly

indicators.note: seizing means the savage word grabs and holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: savage and vicious both mean fierce and violent

indicators.note: heads of picks the first letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fierce, lively person grabs the leaders of a village meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads of' gives V and A from village and assembly, which sit inside VICIOUS after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone full of energy and spirited animation.

clue.text: Empty tubular vessel, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a vein is a tube carrying blood

explanation.surface: A hollow tube vessel, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain means empty or futile, as in a vain hope.

clue.text: Woman's area in 1 ac, old S American port

parts.note: Val is a woman's name

indicators.note: in means the area letter goes inside the answer to 1 across

parts.note: 1 across is the French capital

explanation.surface: A woman's district in Paris, then an old South American harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Wait for 1 across: its answer has A inserted after PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Valparaiso is a long-established port city on the coast of Chile.

clue.text: Exactly what's needed in rodent's hole

indicators.note: in means the needed-thing word sits inside the rodent word

parts.note: a cavy is a guinea pig, a South American rodent
it means just the thing, as in that's it

explanation.surface: A rodent's burrow is exactly what it needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is a hollow space or hole.

clue.text: Plant expert reprimanded during organised riots

indicators.note: during means the reprimanded word comes in the middle of the rearranged letters
organised means the letters of riots are arranged afresh

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to reprimand

explanation.surface: A botanist was told off during organised rioting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges riots, and 'during' puts CHID, an archaic past tense of chide, into the middle of that.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchidist is a grower or specialist in orchids, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Shoot an indefinite number out of season

indicators.note: out of means the number letter is removed from the season word

parts.note: spring is a season
n stands for an indefinite number in maths

explanation.surface: A shoot appears out of season, in some number.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig of a plant.

clue.text: Just pass on, finally rejecting the odds

parts.note: to impart is to pass on knowledge or news

indicators.note: rejecting the odds means throwing away the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Advice to give up when the odds look hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like an adverb but is the fodder: its even letters are I, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A just judge is fair and unbiased, taking no side.

clue.text: Minister caught entering through door at rear

indicators.note: entering means the caught letter goes inside the word for through

parts.note: via means by way of, through
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: at rear picks the final letter of the word door

explanation.surface: A clergyman is caught slipping in by the back door.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest, a minister of the Church of England.

clue.text: Like Scot swimming with daughter? I'll say!

parts.note: a swimming Scot might be in the Dee, a river of north-east Scotland

explanation.surface: A jokey question about a Scottish swimmer with his daughter, answered emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a Scottish river flowing to Aberdeen, so a Scot swimming is IN DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic interjections expressing strong agreement or surprise.

clue.text: Distant object once of minimal value

parts.note: far means distant
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Something far away is described as having been nearly worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The farthing was a British coin worth a quarter of an old penny, withdrawn in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: The old quarter-penny coin was the lowest-value British coin, a byword for worthlessness.

clue.text: Sing a carol unexpectedly accompanied by this?

definitions.text: Sing a carol unexpectedly accompanied by this?

indicators.note: unexpectedly means the letters of the carol phrase come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A carol is sung to an unusual accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a carol might be accompanied by this woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is an orchestral woodwind instrument that might accompany singing.

clue.text: Dubliner who distracted soldier with flag?

parts.note: the flag, or yellow flag, is a kind of iris plant

indicators.note: distracted means the letters of who are thrown into confusion

parts.note: a man is an ordinary soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Asks which Dublin native put a soldier off his stride with a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distracted' turns WHO into HWO. 'flag' suggests a banner but is the iris flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman from Dublin is an Irish woman, Dublin being Ireland's capital.

clue.text: Better to eat one's jam?

indicators.note: to eat means the better word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to better is to improve
one's is I'S, i.e. I plus s

explanation.surface: Is it better to eat one's jam?
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' is the jazz verb, to play freely, not a preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To jam in jazz is to play spontaneously, making it up as you go.

clue.text: Lean over border

definitions.meaning: a ship ... when it leans to one side
an edge or selvage strip of cloth

explanation.definitionFit: List means both a tilt to one side and a border strip of fabric.

clue.text: One imparting history finally covering king's betrayal

indicators.note: covering means the teacher word wraps around the king letter

parts.note: a teacher imparts knowledge
R is short for rex, king

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of history

explanation.surface: A history teacher at last covers a king's betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside TEACHER after T; Y from 'history finally' is tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is betrayal of trust.

clue.text: Peacekeepers remain, willingly displaying scepticism

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, sends peacekeepers
to be is to exist or remain
lief is an archaic word for willingly, as in I'd as lief

explanation.surface: UN peacekeepers stay on willingly but show doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbelief is lack of faith, doubt or scepticism.

clue.text: Former American writer cut trade fair

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: cut tells us to drop the last letter of the writer's name

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer of tales and poems

explanation.surface: A one-time American author has been dropped from a trade show.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is a short name for an exposition, a large trade exhibition.

clue.text: Converted semi at Eton providing accommodation

indicators.note: converted means the letters of the fodder are rebuilt in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A semi-detached house near Eton has been converted into rented rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi' here is a British semi-detached house, which fits the property surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a self-contained flat on two floors, a form of housing.

clue.text: Injured party's energy overwhelming island court

indicators.note: overwhelming means the energy word engulfs the other pieces

parts.note: vim is energy

explanation.surface: The injured party's energy overwhelms the island court.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is someone who has been harmed or injured.

clue.text: Low circles where cats may be secured

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
rings are circles

explanation.surface: Lowing cattle in circles, with cats tied up somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cats' are catboats or catamarans, not felines; 'Low' is the cow's sound, not short.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorings are the places where boats are tied up, and cats are small boats.

clue.text: Second section of poem set up recurring idea

parts.note: mo is a short moment or second

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a fit is an old word for a canto, a section of a poem

explanation.surface: The second section of a poem sets up a recurring theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring theme or idea in art or music.

clue.text: Heartily sick at church officer's a language

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

indicators.note: heartily means take the heart, the central letters, of the word sick

explanation.surface: A church officer's language is said to be thoroughly sickening.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic is the family of languages including Irish, Welsh and Breton.

clue.text: Unqualified soldiers invading rising piece of land in America

indicators.note: invading means the soldiers go inside the land word
rising in a down clue means the land word is read upwards

parts.note: a lot is the American word for a plot of land
the TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Unqualified troops invade a plot of land in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the American land word, since this is a down clue; the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Total means absolute or unqualified, as in total failure.

clue.text: Willing to receive such a verdict?

definitions.meaning: receptive and unguarded, as in amenable to offers
an inquest may return a verdict leaving the cause of death undetermined

explanation.definitionFit: Open means receptive, and an open verdict leaves the cause undecided.

clue.text: Change of direction tour leader was aware of

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word tour

parts.note: wist is the archaic past tense of wit, to know

explanation.surface: A tour guide knew all about the sudden change of route.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is a sudden turn or bend, as in a twist in the road.

clue.text: Tailless dog kept by primate's new member of staff

indicators.note: kept by means the dog sits inside the primate word

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the dog word is cut off

parts.note: a pointer is a gun dog

explanation.surface: An ape keeps a dog with no tail as its new hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' drops the dog's final R; 'primate's' looks possessive but is simply the container word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone appointed to a post is a newly appointed employee.

clue.text: Brother following team regularly visiting grounds

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: visiting means these letters go inside the grounds word

parts.note: grounds for an action are its reason

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of team, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A brother follows his team, regularly going to their grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' is how Freemasons address one another; 'regularly' takes the even letters of team, and 'visiting' puts them inside the grounds word.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Masonic order address one another as Brother.

clue.text: Part of idyll offhand about mock Gothic building

indicators.note: about tells us the run is then read backwards
part of signals that the letters lie in a run across idyll offhand

explanation.surface: A section of a casual idyll is about a fake Gothic structure.
explanation.walkthrough: The run YLLOF spans 'idyll offhand' and reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A folly is an ornamental garden building, often a sham ruin or tower.
